purpose: BrainVolumeRefinement provides one C++ CLI module, BVeR. It iteratively removes over-segmented non-brain voxels from the border of an already skull-stripped brain MRI volume. It is meant for neuroimaging researchers who use FSL-BET, FreeSurfer or similar tools.
summary: I read all the C++ source, the XML, the CMake files, the docs and the LICENSE. The extension is a self-contained ITK CLI with no network access, no Python, no package installs, no downloads and no file operations beyond the user-specified outputs. I found no safety or environment concerns. The license is Apache 2.0, and the catalog entry (scm_revision "main", no dependencies) looks usable. The main problems are soundness bugs: uninitialized accumulators drive the convergence criterion, and the output can be blank if the loop exits early. There are also template leftovers: a test that passes a non-existent --sigma option, an MIT/Apache license mismatch in the docs, and placeholder text in the XML. These are non-blocking.
